data.long_meaning: From the Old German elements hrod meaning 'fame' and landan meaning 'land'. The name Roldan was popular among the Germanic tribes and was borne by several early Christian saints. It was also a common name among the Anglo-Saxons and the Normans. The name Roldan carries the meaning “Ruler, Soldier” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Roldan usually hope their child will grow to embody ruler, soldier and live with faith, good character and purpose.

The name Roldan evokes images of royalty, power, and dominance, reflecting the proud and noble heritage of the Germanic people. Some of the greatest rulers in history bore this name, reflecting the spirit of leadership and resilience embedded in the name.
data.spiritual_significance: Roldan is a name deeply rooted in the traditions of the early Christian Church. Several saints by this name have contributed significantly to the spiritual growth of Europe during the Middle Ages. Saint Roldan, a Breton saint, is known for his miraculous healings and intercessions, particularly in matters related to fertility and marriage. Another Saint Roldan, a Frankish saint, is renowned for his religious zeal and his contributions towards the spread of Christianity. The name Roldan exemplifies the spiritual qualities of strength, integrity, and unwavering faith, inspired by the namesakes who lived by these virtues.
